title: Fantasy football, week by week
text:
What this is
A bot that watches your ESPN fantasy league.
It talks in Discord. It also keeps a website of the season.
You do not start it on game day. It is already running.

The container stays up all season. League members only need Discord and a browser. No one has to remember a schedule or log into ESPN to see the same numbers.

title: Fantasy football, week by week
text:
Three things you get



Channel


Scheduled posts

Scoreboards, matchups, standings, and trophies land in Discord on their own.



Anytime


Slash commands

Type a command in the server when you want the current week, not the last post.



The season


Web dashboard

Charts, records, and season awards from every week the bot has saved.



These are the only three surfaces. Scheduled posts use a webhook. Slash commands need the bot invited to the server. The dashboard is a web page, local or on a public URL.

title: Fantasy football, week by week
text:
What shows up in Discord
Each post is one report. Typical reports:

Current scores and projections
Close games
Final scores and weekly trophies
Power rankings and standings
Thursday matchups
Waiver moves
Sunday injury watch


The tone matches ESPN’s own reports: names, scores, ranks. Private leagues need ESPN cookies before waiver moves appear. Public leagues skip that report.

title: Fantasy football, week by week
text:
Ask the bot yourself
Type / in Discord. Pick a command:


/matchups this week’s games
/scoreboard live scores
/standings the table
/power-rankings who is hot
/monitor injuries
/trophies this week’s awards
/waiver-report adds and drops
/dashboard link to the site



Commands read ESPN live. The dashboard reads the saved season. If they disagree on year, the dashboard is behind until the next Tuesday snapshot, or until someone backfills a prior season.

title: Fantasy football, week by week
text:
The dashboard
A dark page of the whole season, opening on what just happened.

Lands on This week: results, movers, and everyone against their own average
Scope League and Records: regular season, playoffs, or the full season
Pick a season if more than one is saved
Click a team anywhere. You land on its own page, every chart scoped to it

The page refreshes itself about every 30 seconds.

Empty dashboard means no snapshot has run yet. A completed past season can be loaded with the backfill script. League members never need that command; it is a maintainer step.

title: Fantasy football, week by week
text:
Four destinations



This week

Scores, movers, and week bests. The front page, no configuring required.



League

A readable standings board, plus the one chart with ten lines: the race.



Teams

One page per team: game log, range vs the league, and every head-to-head.



Records

The record book. Every row is a click into the team it belongs to.



Five tabs became four. Trend’s rank view moved into League as “the race.” Spread and head to head moved into Teams, scoped to one team instead of ten at once. Trophies became Records, a ledger instead of a card grid.

title: Fantasy football, week by week
text:
The record book
Twelve awards, not a single champion graphic.
Highest score. Closest game. Biggest blowout. Luckiest win.
Click a row. You land on that team’s page, ready to dig further.

This is the feature people remember. The old version showed the award and stopped. Now every row is a way into a team’s own page.

Where it started




The first working version of this dashboard: light theme, a sidebar, four stat boxes, four tabs. Same underlying data as every version since. Worth keeping around as a reminder of how far a Shiny Express app can travel without ever touching the numbers underneath it.

title: Fantasy football, week by week
text:
What you do
Nothing on Sunday morning.
Open Discord for the latest post, or type a slash command.
Open the dashboard when you want the season, not the week.

If someone asks how to log in: they don’t. Discord is the league server they already belong to. The dashboard is https://fantasy.ethandbard.com/, or localhost:8000 on the host machine.

Where to read more
The longer write-up is the same site at two URLs:

https://fantasy-docs.ethandbard.com/ — the URL to share
https://ethandbard.github.io/fantasy-football/ — GitHub Pages

The dashboard is separate. That lives at https://fantasy.ethandbard.com/.

The custom hostname is the one to send people. GitHub Pages is the origin copy. The live league dashboard is a different host: the Shiny app behind Cloudflare Tunnel, not these static files.

title: Fantasy football, week by week
text:
How that write-up updates
Push to main. A GitHub Action renders docs/ onto the gh-pages branch.
GitHub Pages serves one URL from that branch.
A Cloudflare Worker fetches that copy for the custom hostname.
A content change needs a push. Redeploy the Worker only if proxy-worker.js changes.

The Action is .github/workflows/quarto-publish.yml. Wrangler deploy from docs/ is only for the Worker script. The two docs URLs stay in sync because the Worker does not store its own HTML.

title: League updates in Discord. The season on a dashboard.
text:
ESPN fantasy football




One Docker container posts ESPN reports on a schedule, answers slash commands, and serves a web dashboard of league history.

Score updates





Set DAILY_WAIVER to True to post the waiver report every day at 9:01 AM, not only Wednesday. The matchup polls are native Discord polls, one per matchup, open for MATCHUP_POLL_HOURS (65 by default, closing before Sunday’s early games); set MATCHUP_POLLS to False to skip them. The Tuesday snapshot waits until Monday night football is final. A trade check also runs every hour, every day: each trade is announced once, within the hour it clears.

title: League updates in Discord. The season on a dashboard.
text:
Dashboard
The dashboard reads data/fantasy.db. It does not call ESPN on its own. It opens on This week, the latest collected week for the season. League and Records carry a scope segment — Regular, Playoffs, or Full — that sets which weeks are in play. The regular-season boundary comes from the data. A team’s wins plus losses plus ties is how many games it has played.


This week
Results ordered closest-first, who moved in the standings, the week’s bests, and every team against its own average. Below them, the week’s recap: a few hundred words written by the league recap agent on Tuesday morning, game by game, with a note on the standings and the week’s moves. It appears on its own once the agent has written it. Nothing to configure.


League
The standings board — record, streak, last-five form, points for/against, and a sparkline per row — sortable by seed, points, or recent form. Below it: luck (all-play record and expected wins, with a points-for against points-against quadrant), playoff odds from a simulation of the remaining schedule, projection accuracy per team, the head-to-head grid, the trade and moves ledgers, the week’s power rankings written by the agent, and “the race”: rank by week for every team on one chart.


Teams
One page per team: average, ceiling, floor, projection delta, and points for and against with their league rank; a week-by-week bar chart against the league average; where the points come from by position; bench regrets (the optimal lineup each week against the one started, and the losses that were left on the bench); a game log; range vs the league; and every head-to-head matchup for that team, sorted by average margin. The agent’s own team page also carries a manager’s log of the moves it made and why. The full head-to-head grid stays on the League page.


Players
Leaderboards from every played week’s lineups: points as a starter, starts, average, best week, and boom and bust rates, filterable by position. Every rostered player counts, bench weeks included.


Records
The record book. Twelve season awards, each a row with its scoreline and week, that links straight to the team it belongs to, the all-time book keyed on (year, week), and the champions once a season’s bracket is played out.


Chat
A data chat for league members, behind a shared passphrase. It answers from the site’s own tables (scores, standings, head to head, records, lineups, the draft, trades, moves) with a small model and per-viewer daily caps. It does not give start, sit, or trade advice; that is what /ask in Discord is for, and it says so.


Selecting a team — a standings row, a matchup, a record-book row, or the team picker itself — takes you to that team’s own page rather than filtering a shared chart. The dashboard has no reset button because there is nothing left to un-filter: each destination shows the whole league, or one team, never a muted version of either.
A dropdown in the masthead selects the season. Only seasons in the database appear there. The page polls the database every 30 seconds, so a new snapshot reaches an open tab on its own, advancing This week’s default view along with it.
Reach the dashboard at http://localhost:8000 locally, or at https://fantasy.ethandbard.com/.

title: League updates in Discord. The season on a dashboard.
text:
How it runs
The entrypoint gamedaybot/run.py starts three parts in one process:





flowchart LR
  ESPN["ESPN API"] --> Bot["fantasy-bot container"]
  Bot --> Hook["Discord webhook"]
  Bot --> Slash["Slash-command bot"]
  Bot --> DB["SQLite in data/"]
  DB --> Dash["Shiny dashboard :8000"]
  Dash --> Tunnel["Cloudflare Tunnel"]







A scheduler posts recurring reports to a Discord webhook.
A Discord gateway bot answers slash commands, if DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN is set.
A Shiny dashboard on port 8000, backed by SQLite in data/.

A Cloudflare tunnel publishes the dashboard. On the VPS that is the shared connector on the edge network. Off the VPS it is an optional cloudflared sidecar with its own tunnel credentials. DASHBOARD_URL in config.env is the link /dashboard returns.
Secrets stay in config.env. Docker Compose loads them through env_file, so no secret is baked into the image.

title: League updates in Discord. The season on a dashboard.
text:
Preview and publish this site
The overview and slides are a Quarto website in docs/.
Preview:
quarto preview docs
Render:
quarto render docs
Output lands in docs/_site. Two public URLs serve that folder:







URL
How it is served




https://ethandbard.github.io/fantasy-football/
GitHub Pages, from the gh-pages branch


https://fantasy-docs.ethandbard.com/
A Cloudflare Worker that fetches the GitHub Pages copy



Push to main to publish content. The workflow in .github/workflows/quarto-publish.yml renders docs/ and deploys docs/_site to gh-pages. GitHub Pages serves that branch. The Worker at the custom hostname fetches the same GitHub Pages site. Both URLs then show the new render.
The Worker script is proxy-worker.js in this directory. Redeploy it only when that file changes:
cd docs
npx wrangler deploy
A change to the Quarto pages does not need wrangler deploy. Push to main is enough.
Do not run a second copy of the bot stack on another host at the same time. Two schedulers post every report twice. The docs site has no such limit: it is static files only.
